claims.explanation: Trichostatin A is a pan-HDAC inhibitor whose selectivity is best explained by the dependence of tumor cells on HDAC-containing corepressor complexes, particularly those involving RB/E2F and NuRD/CoREST chromatin remodeling. Lines with intact RB1 and functional SWI/SNF (ARID1A/SMARCA4) are more sensitive because HDAC inhibition derepresses E2F and lineage-specific enhancers, while loss of RB1 or SWI/SNF components or high expression of HDAC6/HDAC2 can buffer the drug's effects. TP53 mutation is nearly ubiquitous and therefore not discriminative, but co-occurring activating BRAF/NRAS/MAPK or PIK3CA/PTEN alterations may further sensitize by increasing dependence on HDAC-mediated transcriptional programs.

features.basis: RB1 loss reduces HDAC1 recruitment to E2F promoters, blunting TSA-induced derepression (PMID 9468139)
ARID1A-mutant lines are enriched among sensitive lines, suggesting SWI/SNF loss increases HDAC dependence
SMARCA4-mutant lines appear among resistant lines, consistent with SWI/SNF-independent chromatin buffering
BRAF-mutant melanomas and other lineages are enriched in the sensitive set, possibly via MAPK-driven HDAC dependence
NRAS-mutant lines are enriched among sensitive lines, suggesting MAPK pathway activation sensitizes to HDAC inhibition
HDAC6 is upregulated by TSA in the virtual cell, and high baseline HDAC6 may buffer tubulin/HSF1-related effects
Higher HDAC2 expression could require higher intracellular TSA concentrations to fully inhibit deacetylation
TP53 mutation is nearly universal in sensitive lines but also common in resistant lines, so it is weak evidence
PIK3CA-mutant lines appear in the sensitive set, possibly reflecting PI3K-driven HDAC dependence
PTEN loss appears in several resistant lines, suggesting PI3K/AKT activation may reduce HDAC inhibitor sensitivity
KMT2D-mutant lines are enriched among sensitive lines, possibly via altered enhancer H3K4 methylation and HDAC reliance
EP300 mutation appears in both sensitive and resistant lines, but loss of p300 acetyltransferase may reduce the impact of deacetylation balance
